articles.title: ‘I’m in a bad place’: Mark Allen says his snooker career may be over after defeat
articles.summary: Former world No 1 loses 4-2 to Jordan Brown in Belfast. ‘I don’t see a future with snooker in it,’ says tearful Allen. Mark Allen said he was in a “bad place” and his snooker career could be over after losing to Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast.
body: The 40-year-old was playing his first match since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April. Allen missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose the deciding frame to Wu, who went on to win the title.

Allen has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private – although they are understood not to relate directly to his Crucible defeat. After his 4-2 loss to Brown, a close friend who is also from Antrim, Allen indicated he is set to take another long break from the sport – and could make it permanent.
In an emotional interview with TNT Sports after the match, Allen said he was “really overwhelmed,” adding: “I’m in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough.”

“I think if I wasn’t playing Jordan I wouldn’t have come back,” the former world No 1 said. “I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates – I thought that was a better way to sign out.”

articles.title: Vincent Kompany may miss Bayern’s clash with Arsenal due to legs-affecting virus
articles.summary: Kompany told to rest after struggling with infection. His assistant poised to oversee Champions League game. Vincent Kompany is touch and go to be in the Bayern Munich dugout against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night as he battles a debilitating virus that has affected his legs.
body: Kompany has been told to rest after he struggled through Bayern’s 6-1 home win over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the viral infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk.

“It has affected his legs at times,” Danks confirmed. “He’s felt some pain in his legs. I’m not sure about the reports about him lying down on the couch. I think we can all have a lie down on the couch after a game. It’s just a virus. The doctors and experts know way more than I do. The most important thing we have encouraged is that he rests; he takes the time he needs – however long that may be.

“Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more – whether that’s tomorrow or whether that’s two or three days’ time. I don’t know. We just take it day-by-day and see how he is. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge. You know him as a person. He’s a real leader. He works hard.”

articles.title: Turkish FA bans 147 officials for breaching betting rules
articles.summary: Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan is among 147 club officials given a 45-day ban by the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) for breaching betting rules.
body: In September, it was announced 448 people had been provisionally suspended and referred to the TFF's professional football disciplinary board over allegations they had placed bets while in office.
Like players and coaches, match officials are forbidden from participating in betting activities by TFF regulations, as well as those of Fifa and Uefa.
The TFF said the people involved had held posts at clubs in the top two divisions in Turkish football over the previous five years.
Of those, some 147 were found to have breached betting rules and will be barred from carrying out duties within football during the suspension period.

articles.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
articles.summary: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup. DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland. Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field.
body: The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history.

The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco.
“I wasn’t aware [we were breaking a record], but I’m super proud of this group and it’s nice that they have something like that behind their name,” US coach Ciara Crinion told Fifa’s website.

DiMaria, a 17-year-old high-schooler from St Louis who is committed to play in college at North Carolina, scored her first goal 63 minutes into the match. It was the most goals by a US player ever in any match and the most by any player in a Women’s World Cup match at any level.

articles.title: Webb backs VAR over Botman challenge on Jackson
articles.summary: Premier League referees' chief Howard Webb says Sven Botman's challenge on Nicolas Jackson was a "high-end reckless challenge" but backed the video assistant referee's decision not to intervene for a red card.
body: Botman was shown a yellow card - the correct sanction for a reckless tackle - by referee Jarred Gillett for the Newcastle centre-back's 18th minute challenge on Villa striker Nicolas Jackson on Saturday.
The Dutch defender went in strongly and over the top of the ball, though contact on the opponent was with his trailing leg.
"I think it's reckless," Gillett said of the challenge. "Even though you get a touch on the ball, it's still reckless."
The VAR, Stuart Attwell, decided to support the on-field call of a caution because there was "no secondary scissor action" and contact was "not with the studs".

articles.title: Allen considers retirement after NI Open exit
articles.summary: Mark Allen says that retiring from snooker is "something I have been contemplating for a while" following his 4-2 loss to Jordan Brown in the Northern Ireland Open.
body: Allen was beaten 4-2 by fellow Antrim man Brown in his first event since losing to Wu Yize in heartbreaking fashion during the semi-finals of the World Championship in Sheffield in May.
The former world number one said showing up to play his match against Brown was an "achievement" after a "really difficult" period in his life while he took a break from competitive action.
"I think if I hadn't have been playing Jordan, I probably would not have played," Allen told BBC Sport NI after his defeat at the Waterfront Hall in Belfast.
"I felt like I did not want my last match to be remembered for that semi-final in Sheffield.

articles.summary: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has full confidence in CEO Ed Coetzee, rejecting claims of "executive-level chaos".
body: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee and dismissed a newspaper article suggesting there was "executive-level chaos" at the club.
In an open letter on Saracens' website, external, responding to an article in The Times last week, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July.
"The board has full confidence in Ed and his team," Silvester wrote.

"We believe they have the experience, capability and determination to raise standards across every area of the club, strengthen our financial sustainability and ensure that Saracens continues to be an organisation of which our players, staff, partners and supporters can be proud."

articles.title: Why did OU football leave OL Ryan Fodje in game despite injury? Ben Arbuckle explains
articles.summary: OU football offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle was asked Tuesday to further clarify why offensive lineman Ryan Fodje remained in the Kentucky game after suffering an injury.
body: NORMAN — In the immediate aftermath of Saturday’s loss to Kentucky, questions swirled around why Oklahoma left offensive lineman Ryan Fodje in the game so long when he was clearly injured.

“Whenever he got a little bit banged up there at the end, I was told that the injury couldn’t get any worse,” Arbuckle said. “And again, with some of the limitations that we did have, had him out there.”

Down Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis, OU was already trying to piece together a battered and bruised unit. But once Fodje got hurt in the third quarter, the Sooners’ offense fell apart.
He gave up two sacks in the fourth quarter during a critical drive before OU ultimately pulled him.

articles.title: 'Appalling' batting and 'wickets in clumps' leave England with ODI setback
articles.summary: England captain Harry Brook admits his side were 'too careful' against Pakistan’s spinners after collapsing to a disappointing 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener.
body: Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.
"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.
